Get prescribing totals from OpenPrescribing

Source: R/openprescribing.R
get_op_spending.Rd

Retrieves monthly prescribing items, quantity and actual cost (GBP) for one or more BNF codes from the OpenPrescribing API, aggregated to the spatial resolution you choose. The data are NHS England primary-care (mainly GP) prescriptions dispensed in the community, from the English Prescribing Dataset; the API holds the most recent five years.

Usage

get_op_spending(
  code,
  resolution = "england",
  org = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  combine = FALSE,
  add_list_size = FALSE,
  as_data_table = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

code

character vector of BNF codes or section numbers (see Details). Optionally named to set labels.

resolution

spatial resolution: one of "england" (default), "region", "icb", "sicbl", "pcn", "practice".

org

optional character vector of organisation codes to keep (for example ICB codes). For resolution = "practice" a Sub-ICB code expands to all of its practices. NULL (default) returns every organisation at that resolution. Find codes with search_op_org.

date

optional month(s) to return: Date objects or "YYYY-MM-DD" / "YYYY-MM" strings. Any day is rounded down to the first of its month.

start, end

optional first and last month (inclusive) as for date; either may be given alone. Not combinable with date.

combine

logical. If TRUE, all codes are summed in a single request (the API treats multiple codes as a union) and returned as one series. Beware double counting if the codes overlap.

add_list_size

logical. If TRUE, also fetch get_op_org_details and add total_list_size and items_per_1000 (items per 1,000 registered patients).

as_data_table

logical; return a data.table.

verbose

logical; message the number of requests when it is large.

Value

A data.frame with one row per month and organisation (and code):

date

first day of the month (Date).

resolution

the canonical resolution requested.

org_id, org_name

organisation code and name (NA / "england" for national totals).

code, code_label

the BNF code (or comma-joined codes if combine) and its label.

items

number of prescription items.

quantity

total quantity dispensed (units depend on the presentation, so only compare within the same product).

actual_cost

actual cost in GBP.

Practice-level results add parent_sicbl and setting (the practice setting code; 4 is a standard GP practice). With add_list_size, columns total_list_size and items_per_1000 are appended. Months with no prescribing for an organisation are omitted by the API, not returned as zero.

Spatial resolutions

"england"

one national series (the default).

"region"

NHS England regions (the API's regional_team).

"icb"

Integrated Care Boards (the API's stp).

"sicbl"

Sub-ICB Locations (the API's ccg).

"pcn"

Primary Care Networks.

"practice"

individual GP practices.

"stp", "ccg", "sub-icb" and "regional_team" are accepted as aliases. Organisations are those currently defined by OpenPrescribing: practice prescribing is attributed to the organisation the practice belongs to now, so a series does not follow past mergers or boundary changes. Check that the org_id values match the boundary vintage you plan to join them to.

BNF codes

code is matched as a prefix, so "0501" covers all of BNF section 5.1 (antibacterial drugs) and "0501013B0" a single chemical. Section numbers such as "5.1" or "5.1.1" are also accepted. If you supply several codes they are fetched separately (one API request each) and returned in long format with a code column, unless combine = TRUE. Names on code become the code_label column. Find codes with search_op_bnf or op_antibiotic_classes.

Request volume

National and organisation-level queries need one request per code. The API will not return all practices for all months in one call, so resolution = "practice" without org needs date or both start and end and sends one request per code per month. All requests are throttled to getOption("ukhsadatR.requests_per_second", 1).

See also

get_op_antibiotics, get_op_org_details, get_op_boundaries

Examples

# \donttest{
# All antibacterials (BNF 5.1), England, monthly
get_op_spending("0501")
#> Error: OpenPrescribing refused the request (HTTP 403, a bot-protection challenge), so no data could be retrieved from /spending_by_org/.
#> This is applied by the service to some networks and clients (for example some cloud or institutional IP ranges). Try again later or from another network, and consider reducing the request rate with options(ukhsadatR.requests_per_second = 0.5).

# Penicillins and macrolides by ICB for 2024, with rates per 1,000 patients
get_op_spending(
  c(Penicillins = "050101", Macrolides = "050105"),
  resolution = "icb", start = "2024-01", end = "2024-12",
  add_list_size = TRUE
)
#> Error: OpenPrescribing refused the request (HTTP 403, a bot-protection challenge), so no data could be retrieved from /spending_by_org/.
#> This is applied by the service to some networks and clients (for example some cloud or institutional IP ranges). Try again later or from another network, and consider reducing the request rate with options(ukhsadatR.requests_per_second = 0.5).

# One chemical (amoxicillin) in every practice of one Sub-ICB, one month
sicbl <- search_op_org("devon", resolution = "sicbl")$code[1]
#> Error: OpenPrescribing refused the request (HTTP 403, a bot-protection challenge), so no data could be retrieved from /org_code/.
#> This is applied by the service to some networks and clients (for example some cloud or institutional IP ranges). Try again later or from another network, and consider reducing the request rate with options(ukhsadatR.requests_per_second = 0.5).
get_op_spending("0501013B0", resolution = "practice", org = sicbl,
                date = "2024-06")
#> Error: object 'sicbl' not found
# }
